scope: Primary sources checked live for the finite-data estimator and matched-baseline comparison. Source statements are literature reports, not independent verification of the papers' theorems.

sources.citation: Jannik Ehrich, Tightest bound on hidden entropy production from partially observed dynamics
accessed_ranges: lines 88-89: long trajectory and ergodicity assumption for estimating statistics
lines 110-151: observed path irreversibility is a lower bound; waiting-time/jump statistics estimator
lines 227-229: hidden-network fitting assumes the correct number of hidden states is known
lines 284-295: model fitting uses all observable statistics, is tighter in the stated example, and needs accurate data/known hidden count
claims_used: Observed path reversal KL is an established model-independent lower bound and can be zero despite hidden dissipation.
Waiting-time and hidden-model-fit methods use richer trajectory statistics; the cited hidden-fit construction assumes known hidden-state count and has substantial data requirements.

sources.citation: Eden Nitzan, Aishani Ghosal, and Gili Bisker, Universal bounds on entropy production inferred from observed statistics
accessed_ranges: lines 70-76: comparison classes including stalling and waiting-time KLD estimators
lines 120-122 and 162-168: minimization over underlying models with the hypothesized same topology and matching observed statistics
lines 217-220: molecular-motor stalling comparison and long-trajectory simulation statistics
lines 223-228: sensitivity to statistical accuracy, constraint tolerance, and problem size
claims_used: A topology-informed estimator can be stronger when a hidden topology/model class is supplied and observed transition/waiting-time statistics are matched.
The literature reports a tight positive optimized bound at a visible-current stall in its molecular-motor example; this is not a same-ring comparison.

sources.citation: Paul Raux, Alexander M. Maier, and Udo Seifert, Lower bounds on entropy production from dynamical correlation functions
accessed_ranges: lines 86-98: definition of two-time correlation asymmetry chi
lines 150-175: NESS lower bound proportional to chi squared and valid for arbitrary lag
lines 177-194: separate vanishing-lag result for time-dependent processes
claims_used: The cited two-time-asymmetry bound vanishes when the complete observed stationary path law is invariant under reversal, because then all corresponding chi values vanish.

sources.citation: Andreas Maurer and Massimiliano Pontil, Empirical Bernstein Bounds and Sample Variance Penalization
accessed_ranges: lines 81-89: one-sided empirical Bernstein bound and pairwise sample-variance formula
lines 90-98: finite-class simultaneous extension with log(2|F|/delta)
claims_used: The holdout confidence interval follows the cited IID empirical-Bernstein result after rescaling X from [-1,1] to [0,1]; the factor 14 in the additive term is due to this rescaling.

sources.citation: Palle Jorgensen and Feng Tian, Reflection positivity and spectral theory
accessed_ranges: lines 43-46: Markov property implies reflection positivity in the authors' operator-theoretic setup, but not conversely
claims_used: This source motivates the caution that a reflection-positivity condition alone is not a complete Markov-generator characterization; it is not used as a direct proof about the finite observed pair table.
